subject: NovaPay onboarding: benchmark certification & surge test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@novapay.com>, Noah Kim <noah.kim@novapay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: NovaPay onboarding: benchmark certification & surge test plan

Hi Elena / Noah,

Thanks again for the sync yesterday — this thread is to capture the proposed certification plan for NovaPay's Redwood onboarding and to lock acceptance criteria so our CS and infra teams can schedule the load runs. Attached is the working workbook with the detailed run matrix (novapay-surge-test-plan.xlsx). High level plan below: 

- Goal: Validate production SLOs under expected peak and 2x surge for core payment inference flows (tokenization + fraud-score chat).
- Primary metrics: median token latency, p95 tail latency, tokens/sec throughput, error rate, and model output divergence vs. baseline.
- Acceptance thresholds (proposed):
  - Median token latency <= 12ms
  - p95 latency <= 60ms
  - Sustained throughput >= 18k tokens/sec at target concurrency profile
  - Error rate < 0.5% (server errors/timeouts)
  - Output divergence: BLEU-like delta <= 1.5% vs. reference prompts

Planned timeline:
- Prep & data hang: May 12–13 (instrumentation, runbook review)
- Dry runs (low concurrency): May 14
- Full runs (target + 2x surge): May 15–16
- Results digest and artifacts shared: May 17

Operational notes for the team:
- We'll use Redwood's benchmark harness (see link below) and NovaPay's replay traces (anonymized) to drive realistic request patterns.
- Cache warmup: we recommend a 20-minute steady ramp before measuring to populate KV caches.
- Canary model fallback: if tail latency > 120ms at any point, Redwood will automatically route to the compatible quantized variant; we'll mark those events as failures for certification.

Next steps / asks from NovaPay:
1) Confirm acceptance thresholds above or provide counter-proposals by EOD May 13.
2) Share sanitized request traces (s3 link or attachments) for replay by EOD May 13.
3) Confirm availability window for May 15–16 full runs (4hr contiguous slot preferred).

Attachments: novapay-surge-test-plan.xlsx (run matrix), redwood-benchmark-results-template.csv (artifact template)

Thanks — I looped in Monica and Ben for run ops and telemetry.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Sr Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
From: Elena Rossi <elena@novapay.com>

Cc: Noah Kim <noah.kim@novapay.com>, NovaPay Platform Team <platform@novapay.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovaPay onboarding: benchmark certification & surge test plan

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear plan. A few quick clarifications before we sign off on thresholds: 

1) For throughput: our expected steady-state is ~10k tokens/sec but we need headroom up to 20k during promos. Is the 18k sustained a hard requirement or negotiable?
2) Output divergence: can you remind us which reference prompt set you used for the BLEU-like calculation? We want to ensure it includes multi-turn examples.
3) Can you confirm whether Redwood will capture full per-token timestamps in the artifacts? We need them to validate tail behavior in our analytics.

Availability: we can reserve May 15 afternoon (PST) for the 4hr slot — prefer 13:00–17:00 PT. We'll upload sanitized traces to the S3 folder you shared by EOD May 13.

Thanks — 
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Engineering, NovaPay
elena@novapay.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

Subject: Re: NovaPay onboarding: benchmark certification & surge test plan

Thanks for the quick review, Elena — answers inline and a small tweak to the thresholds based on expected trace mix:

1) Throughput: 18k was a conservative target aligned to your 10k steady state with a headroom buffer. We can set the certification target to 16k sustained and mark 20k as stretch/surge validation.

2) Reference prompts: we used the multi-turn production subset you shared in March (folder: novapay-prod-refset v2). It includes tokenization and multi-turn fraud-score prompts; I'll add a note in the runbook to ensure it remains the canonical reference.

3) Per-token timestamps: yes — Redwood will include per-token timestamps (ISO ms) in the CSV artifact. We’ll also provide a pre-computed tail summary (p50/p90/p95/p99) for quick review.

Updated acceptance thresholds (final proposal):
- Median token latency <= 12ms
- p95 latency <= 60ms
- Sustained throughput >= 16k tokens/sec
- Surge target: 20k tokens/sec for 10 minutes (non-certifying)
- Error rate < 0.5%
- Output divergence <= 1.5%

Schedule: we confirmed May 15 13:00–17:00 PT for full runs. We'll start a 30-min instrumentation check at 12:30 and a 20-minute ramp at 13:00. Dry runs will happen May 14 as planned.

I've attached the updated run matrix (see column "Certification Target" in the spreadsheet). We'll capture artifacts to the shared S3 location and post the result CSV to the runbook link when done.

Please confirm that the updated thresholds work for you and that the team will upload the sanitized traces to s3://novapay-onboard by 23:59 PT May 13.

Thanks —
—Marissa

Date: 2027-05-15T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovaPay onboarding: benchmark certification & surge test plan

Quick run-ops notes from infra before the full run: 

- Cache warmup: plan for a 20–30 minute warmup window. If your traces have high variance in prefixes, expect initial p95 spikes until the KV cache stabilizes. We'll document minute-by-minute p95 during warmup in the artifact CSV.
- Batching: for the numerical inference path we'll apply a dynamic batching window tuned to hit the target throughput while keeping median latency under 12ms; worst-case batching add-on should not exceed +8ms median.
- Failover policy: if we observe >0.5% server error rate for a continuous 5-minute window we will stop the run, capture state, and retry once with the quantized fallback model. That retry run will not count for certification but will be included in artifacts.
- Instrumentation: please ensure the replay traces include header metadata (client_id, route_id) so we can attribute traffic correctly.

I'll be on the call for the May 15 run and will push live telemetry to the shared dashboard.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the clarity and the ops notes. Confirming:

- NovaPay accepts the updated certification thresholds (sustained 16k tokens/sec, p95 <= 60ms, median <= 12ms, error rate < 0.5%).
- We've uploaded sanitized traces to s3://novapay-onboard/trace-v3.tar.gz and added the required header metadata (client_id and route_id).
- We'll join the May 15 12:45 instrumentation check and the 13:00 run start. Noah and I will be on the call to validate the artifact uploads.

Please proceed with the dry run tomorrow (May 14) and the full run on May 15 as scheduled. Once you share the run artifacts on May 17, we'll circulate internally and aim to sign the onboarding certificate the same day if targets are met.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Elena
